summary: This benchmark evaluates cross-model counterfactual activation steering by learning a 25-dimensional linear ridge map from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (block 6) to Qwen2.5-14B (block 10). On a test suite of 512 paired single-letter identifier declarations in Python, the transferred edit achieves a 100% reversal rate while an orthogonal same-norm random perturbation achieves 0%. While the experimental setup includes appropriate negative and positive controls with fully documented software environments and model revisions, the benchmark is constrained to a highly synthetic single-token variable replacement task.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, pairing the translated edit directly against both a full host activation transplant and an orthogonal same-norm random control.
Comprehensive reproducibility metadata provided in-text, including model commit SHAs, library versions (MLX 0.32.4, NumPy 2.5.5, Tokenizers 0.23.3), and exact ridge penalty specifications.
Direct grounding in established model stitching and representation transfer literature (Bansal et al., 2021; Chen et al., 2025).
weaknesses: Extremely narrow evaluation scope restricted to single-character identifier declarations in synthetic Python prompts, leading to saturation/ceiling effects (512/512).
No ablation or sensitivity analysis explaining the choice of layer 6 in the 7B donor and layer 10 in the 14B host over alternative layer combinations.
Brevity of the report omits qualitative inspection of generation degradation or off-target effects outside the targeted completion position.
suggestions: Extend the benchmark to multi-token variable names, function calls, and semantically diverse coding edits to evaluate generalization beyond single-letter swaps.
Provide a layer-to-layer transfer matrix comparing ridge transfer efficacy across all donor-host block pairs to demonstrate why blocks 6 and 10 are optimal.
Measure perplexity or test broader task performance downstream to verify that the injected activation edit does not destabilize general model generation.

claims.text: The coder and general host use widths 3,584 and 5,120.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies linear stitching specifically to low-dimensional counterfactual activation vectors between distinct model architectures and scales rather than full-layer representation concatenation.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Transferring Linear Features Across Language Models With Model Stitching
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses on localized identifier intervention and causal reversal in code synthesis between a 7B domain-specialized coder and a 14B general model using a 25D basis.
